# ARTINEXT, full reference

> ARTINEXT is a digital-systems studio based in Tehran, Iran, working remotely with architecture, structural and MEP teams. Three service lines: custom Revit content, custom digital tools, and office and workflow automation. Every page exists in Persian (`/fa/`, the default) and English (`/en/`) at matching paths.

This file expands on [llms.txt](https://artinext.ir/llms.txt). Everything in it is drawn from copy that appears on the site; nothing here is added.

## Who ARTINEXT is

ARTINEXT works inside the software an office already uses every day. Its time goes to three frictions it finds in almost every office: manual work repeated from memory on every project, data with no single home (quantities, statuses and decisions scattered across files, people and software), and tools that each work on their own but never become one traceable flow from request to report.

The studio's position, stated on the site:

- Every project starts from the client's process, not from a pre-built product. It is not a fit for installing an off-the-shelf template or a generic plugin without a process review, and it says so rather than taking the work.
- There is no price list. A tool is sized by how well the rule is already written down, how many systems it touches, how many people will run it, and what has to happen when it fails. No estimate is given before the problem is stated in full.
- The client owns what gets built. Source and build instructions are handed over.
- If a tool is the wrong answer, the studio says so in the first conversation rather than at the end of a build.
- Work runs remotely by default, in Persian or English, with teams inside and outside Iran.

The process has four stages: **discover** (watch the real workflow, not the documented one), **define** (state the problem in full with a success measure that can be tested, before any tool is proposed), **build** (against the client's standards and users; every added layer of complexity has to earn its place) and **evolve** (systems built to change as the work grows).

Contact: [contact page](https://artinext.ir/en/contact/) · artinext.ai@gmail.com · +98 930 525 3240 · Instagram [@artinext.ir](https://www.instagram.com/artinext.ir/)

## Studio pages

### [Home](https://artinext.ir/en/)
The three frictions above; three product paths (specialist Revit content, custom digital tools, intelligent automation); two tools recorded running inside Revit; the four-stage process; a note on research and development; the technical capabilities behind each path; the latest articles; and common questions (whether they will install a plugin the client already picked: no; where they are based; how a custom tool is priced; starting small; working in Persian and English; what the first conversation covers).

The two recorded tools:
- **C2R (CAD to Revit)** reads a coordinated CAD plan set and creates native Revit elements from it: walls on their real wall types, floors, levels and openings.
- **E2R (ETABS to Revit)** rebuilds an ETABS structural model, from its Excel export, as native Revit framing, and reports per-element counts including what was not created. The figure caption on the home page shows one run: 5,087 members.

### [Products](https://artinext.ir/en/products/)
Three deliverables, each shown as it shipped:
1. **Revit families**: two curtain-wall units from one job that share a frame; only the infill changes. Delivered with proof of behaviour: flexed, scheduled and loaded into a live model.
2. **Digital tools**: the two tools above, recorded running inside Revit, each built around one office's own steps.
3. **Automation**: one system for two offices in two languages, with requests, documents and project status on one screen, delivered running with its process written down.

### [Research and development](https://artinext.ir/en/research-development/)
Staged prototyping in four steps: an idea starts as untested guesses; the first prototype answers one specific question; the measure of success is written before the build and tied to real data; and a prototype ends in one of three outcomes: build it, change part of it, or do not build it.

### [About](https://artinext.ir/en/about/)
The software the studio works in and what it does in each: **Revit** (parametric families, templates, libraries and add-ins), **Navisworks** (clash detection and model review as a repeatable process), **AutoCAD** (standardising existing drawings and keeping 2D connected to the model), **Rhino** (free-form geometry brought back into the model in a usable state), **Grasshopper** (parametric definitions the client's team can run themselves) and **Dynamo** (scripts for repeated jobs inside Revit).

### [Contact](https://artinext.ir/en/contact/)
A project brief form: current process, where it breaks, and the outcome wanted. The first conversation maps the problem and workflow together, assesses the real potential for improvement, and proposes a scope and next step. Request types offered: office and management automation; a custom plugin or tool; a management system or dashboard; BIM, Revit families or modelling; fitting an existing workflow to AI; or an initial review when the need is not yet clear.

## Services

### [Revit plugin development](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-plugin-development/)
Custom Revit plugins and add-ins for architecture, structural and MEP teams, studied against how the team works before any code is written. The three problems plugins are usually bought to fix: a step still done by hand that is fully determined by rules in the office standard; two pieces of software that do not exchange data, with a person retyping between them; and a rule that exists only in someone's head. Questions answered on the page cover Revit version support, working with existing plugins, code ownership, when Dynamo is the better option, and how success is measured before the tool is finished.

### [Revit family creation](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-family-creation/)
Parametric, lightweight families for manufacturers and design offices. Three ways content fails: it flexed once and was called parametric; it is accurate but too heavy to use; it carries no data anyone can schedule. Families are sized by behaviour rather than geometry: how many states they must hold, how clean the source is, what data they must line up with, and whether they ship once or are maintained as a catalogue. Built work: a curtain-wall system delivered as a double-glazed vision unit and a faceted opaque spandrel on one shared frame, brackets and anchor detail. Existing libraries are usually audited and fixed rather than rebuilt.

### [Office automation for AEC companies](https://artinext.ir/en/aec-workflow-automation/)
Office and workflow automation, software and data integration, and operational dashboards for AEC companies and technical offices; nothing here requires Revit. Three signs a process is a candidate: a hand-off that is really a re-typing, a process carried by experience rather than documentation, and daily reports built on data that is already out of date. Built work: one internal dashboard structure delivered to two offices, ARCLINK (Persian, right-to-left, Jalali calendar) and SABER R&D (English), four screens each, running in a browser. The page also covers keeping existing software, handling next year's process changes, where the system runs and who owns it.

### Tehran pages
Each Tehran page offers the same service as its main page, and says what being in the same city changes. None of it is required; projects can run fully remote.
- [Revit plugin development in Tehran](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-plugin-development-tehran/): discovery at the office's own machines, no time difference, handover in person, and shared context on local consultant and submission requirements.
- [Revit family creation in Tehran](https://artinext.ir/en/revit-family-creation-tehran/): the product can be measured rather than inferred, and the first family reviewed in the room with the people who know the product.
- [Office automation in Tehran](https://artinext.ir/en/workflow-automation-tehran/): the process is watched where it happens, step ownership is settled at one table, the system can be installed on the office's own network, and the staff who will use it are trained in person.

## Articles (fa and en, newest first)

Every article carries a named author, a published and updated date, a table of contents, an FAQ section and cited sources. Index: [artinext.ir/en/articles/](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/).

- **[A Revit sheet sorting plugin: from the numbering rule to the issued set](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-sheet-sorting-plugin/)** (2026-09-29). The most dangerous bugs aren't the complicated ones. Covers the two places Revit keeps sheet order (Project Browser with Browser Organization: six grouping levels, sorting, three filter levels; the sheet list with a Sheet Order project parameter), sheet numbers as text and zero padding, Revit's refusal of duplicate sheet numbers and swapping through a temporary number, what a sorting plugin does (numbering rule, preview, conflict-free swaps in one transaction, one shared order, a report of skipped sheets), locking numbers after the first external issue, and off-the-shelf add-in vs Dynamo vs custom plugin.
- **[Revit API development: what you can build, and what a dependable add-in takes](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-api-development/)** (2026-09-29). Stopping when something works is the wrong finish line; stop when you understand it. Covers the Revit API as a .NET library (Elements, FilteredElementCollector, Transactions, decimal-feet internal units), five ways to program Revit (macros, Dynamo, pyRevit, compiled C# add-ins, Design Automation for Revit on Autodesk Platform Services, formerly Forge), IExternalCommand, the .addin manifest, IExternalApplication, TransactionMode and ExternalEvent, what offices build (checks, batch edits, model generation, data exchange, custom MEP add-ins), yearly Revit releases and the .NET 8 recompile in Revit 2025, worksharing, links, failures, scale and reporting, and learning the API vs hiring Revit API development services.
- **[A Revit room finishing automation plugin: what it builds, and the small details that break it](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-room-finishing-automation/)** (2026-09-28). The most dangerous bugs aren't the complicated ones. Covers room finish text parameters (Base, Wall, Floor, Ceiling Finish) vs modelled finish elements, what a plugin builds from SpatialElement.GetBoundarySegments (finish walls with room heights, Floor.Create floors, ceilings, skirting, openings cut at doors, room number on every element), a rule table from room type and host wall type to Revit types, the details that fail (door thresholds, Room Bounding gaps, columns and shafts, unplaced rooms, curved walls), rerunning after design changes via a stored room ID, corner overlaps in takeoff, and off-the-shelf add-in vs Dynamo vs custom plugin.
- **[MVP development for internal tools: the smallest version that answers one question](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/mvp-development-internal-tools/)** (2026-09-28). An MVP that works is half done; it is finished when you understand why it works. Covers the MVP definitions of Eric Ries and Frank Robinson and what changes when the users are your own staff, proof of concept vs prototype vs MVP as three questions, when an internal tool deserves an MVP and when a free trial answers it, writing the question, current state, success measure and stop condition first, cutting scope (keep correct results, unprocessed-item reports and undo), Dynamo or pyRevit as the prototype of a Revit plugin, testing on real files with a parallel run (GOV.UK alpha phase), three outcomes including stopping (Fowler's sacrificial architecture), and upkeep after the MVP.
- **[Software and data integration consulting: draw the data map before choosing a tool](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/software-data-integration-consulting/)** (2026-09-28). The connector is a commodity; the advantage is built in the data map. Covers integration as an agreed rule about ownership and conflicts, the NIST $15.8 billion interoperability figure and the Autodesk/FMI bad-data study, the five-question data map, reference data with a single source, format and conflict rule, four connection methods (scheduled file exchange, direct API, integration layer, shared database), Revit API, IFC and ISO 19650, Persian and Arabic characters, digits and Jalali dates, logging, reconciliation and alerts, and the five deliverables of integration consulting.
- **[A custom AI assistant for business answers from your files, with the source attached](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/custom-ai-assistant-for-business/)** (2026-09-27). A simple interface is compressed history, not a lack of depth. Covers the four parts of a custom assistant (model, sources, retrieval, rules), chatbot vs assistant vs agent, when a licensed product such as Microsoft 365 Copilot or ChatGPT Enterprise is enough, picking one job for one team, retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al., 2020), citations and correct declines against confabulation (NIST AI 600-1), Persian text normalisation and scanned Persian documents, permissions enforced at retrieval, API vs self-hosted models, prompt injection (OWASP LLM01), testing with a known-answer question list, and a six-step build.
- **[A management dashboard for construction companies is only as good as its worst number](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/construction-management-dashboard/)** (2026-09-27). The most dangerous bugs aren't the complicated ones. Covers director, project and operations dashboards, starting from recurring decisions (with Stanford CIFE's 18-KPI set as a contrast), cost, programme, cash, people, document control and safety KPIs, the design-office vs contractor difference (hours against fee), where the numbers live and the Autodesk/FMI bad-data study, KPI definitions, fixed status vocabularies and drill-down to source, refresh rates matched to decisions, Jalali financial year, Saturday week and right-to-left layout, Excel vs Power BI vs a custom build, a staged rollout run in parallel with the manual report, and who keeps it right after launch.
- **[How to prepare company data for AI, starting with the files you already have](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/prepare-company-data-for-ai/)** (2026-09-26). AI is not an advantage before your data is ready. Covers the five properties of AI-ready data, starting from one question, where AEC data actually lives (Revit models, drawing sets, spreadsheets, email), naming and superseded versions, Arabic vs Persian characters and mixed digits as a cleaning problem, ownership and access (NIST AI RMF), and the five outputs of an AI readiness assessment.
- **[A Revit schedule to Excel export plugin is judged by the trip back](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-schedule-to-excel-export/)** (2026-09-26). An export that opens in Excel works; a round trip that knows how Revit stores each value is understood. Covers File, Export, Reports, Schedule (delimited text, not .xlsx), numbers stored as text, what a plugin adds, and five things a round trip must protect: element identity, decimal-feet units, read-only fields, type vs instance parameters, and deleted or added rows.
- **[CAD-to-Revit automation: what a converter builds, and what still needs a person](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/cad-to-revit-automation/)** (2026-09-26). A converter that looks like one button is compressed history. Covers Link CAD vs Import CAD (both an ImportInstance), where manual tracing spends its time, the layer and block standard a drawing set needs, how a converter classifies, pairs, maps, places and reports, Dynamo vs plugin vs conversion service, and why structure and MEP are different problems.
- **[Choosing a Revit plugin development company: what actually matters](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-plugin-development-company/)** (2026-08-29, updated 2026-09-11). The most dangerous problem in a plugin partnership rarely comes from a weak portfolio; it comes from the detail nobody checked. Covers company vs freelancer vs in-house, consulting vs development, the questions to ask before signing, and comparing two quotes on scope rather than total.
- **[Custom Dynamo script development: what it actually replaces](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/custom-dynamo-script-development/)** (2026-08-29, updated 2026-09-11). A graph that runs once on its author's model is an experiment. Covers sheet, data, model-checking and placement graphs; Dynamo Player and named inputs; Python nodes; package versions across Revit upgrades (Revit 2025 ships Dynamo 3.0 on .NET 8); and when a graph should become a compiled add-in.
- **[Where AEC workflow automation should start](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/aec-workflow-automation/)** (2026-08-28, updated 2026-09-11). The ceiling on what is worth automating is usually untested, not real. Covers where offices usually find their first process, three criteria for choosing it, six things to define before automating, data as the real bottleneck (NIST's estimate of $15.8 billion in annual interoperability costs for 2002), a parallel pilot, dashboards tied to one decision, and build vs partner.
- **[Custom parametric Revit family creation: what makes a family actually work](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/custom-parametric-revit-family-creation/)** (2026-08-28, updated 2026-09-11). A family that only flexes once in the editor has proven it worked once. Covers type vs instance parameters, reference planes before geometry, clamping formulas, testing in a real project and schedule, and when a type catalog beats parametric logic.
- **[How much does Revit plugin development cost?](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-plugin-development-cost/)** (2026-08-27, updated 2026-09-11). A plugin that looks like one button is priced by the weeks of work behind it. Cost is driven by workflow complexity, integrations, user count and the Revit versions the tool must support, including the move of the Revit API to .NET 8 in Revit 2025.
- **[A Revit model checker automates QA/QC. It doesn't replace it.](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-model-checker/)** (2026-08-26, updated 2026-09-11). The checkset behind the report is the part worth building. Covers Autodesk's free Model Checker and Configurator (Revit 2023 to 2026), checkset habits, triaging flags, and when a custom Revit API checker is the next step.
- **[Revit library optimization isn't about deleting files](https://artinext.ir/en/articles/revit-library-optimization/)** (2026-08-19, updated 2026-09-11). The most dangerous problem in a library is rarely the biggest file. Covers ArchOverFlow's size guidance (most families under 1 MB, almost all under 3 MB), purging in passes, cleaning downloaded content, object styles, what else weighs a model down, building new families light, upgrading the library once per Revit release, and a quarterly audit.

## Practical notes for automated readers

- The locale is a path segment. `https://artinext.ir/fa/<path>/` and `https://artinext.ir/en/<path>/` are the same page in Persian and English. The bare domain serves the Persian home page.
- Every URL ends in a trailing slash. The canonical tag on each page gives its exact form, and each page links its other-language twin with hreflang.
- The full URL list is in the [sitemap](https://artinext.ir/sitemap.xml). [robots.txt](https://artinext.ir/robots.txt) allows all crawlers.
- Pages from the previous version of the site that were not rebuilt redirect permanently: the Isfahan, Shiraz and Mashhad city pages and the English Canada, UAE and United States pages go to the matching general service page; `/solutions/` goes to the home page; the product subpages go to `/products/`. The Persian pages that targeted Canada, the UAE and the United States were removed on purpose and are gone.
- The site carries no testimonials, client counts, office address or business hours. Figures that do appear, such as the member count in the ETABS to Revit recording, are outputs of real runs.
